translations.idiomatic: In successive years when the emperor went to Mulan, Henan, and Shengjing, Akedun was each time ordered to remain in the capital to manage affairs, acting in turn as Left Censor-in-Chief and Metropolitan Banner Commander.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以目疾乞假，上遣醫視疾。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, citing eye disease, he asked for leave, and the emperor sent a physician to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20, citing eye disease, he asked for leave, and the emperor sent a physician to examine him.

sentences.zh: 屢乞休，命致仕。

translations.literal: He repeatedly asked to retire, and was ordered to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire and was ordered to leave office.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，卒，賜祭葬，諡文勤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died; imperial sacrifices and burial were granted, and he was given the posthumous title Wencqin.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he died; imperial sacrifices and burial were granted, and he was given the posthumous title Wencqin.

sentences.zh: 子阿桂，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Agui has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Agui has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 阿克敦居刑部十餘年，平恕易簡，未嘗有所瞻顧。

translations.literal: Akedun served in the Ministry of Punishments for more than ten years, even-handed, lenient, and straightforward, and never showed favor or hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Akedun served in the Ministry of Punishments for more than ten years, even-handed, lenient, and straightforward, and never showed favor or hesitation.

sentences.zh: 一日，阿桂侍，阿克敦曰：「朝廷用汝為刑官，治獄宜如何？

translations.literal: One day, while Agui was in attendance, Akedun said: "The court has made you a judicial officer—how should cases be handled?
translations.idiomatic: One day, while Agui was in attendance, Akedun said: "The court has made you a judicial officer—how should cases be handled?

sentences.zh: 」阿桂曰：「行法必當其罪，罪一分與一分法，罪十分與十分法。

translations.literal: " Agui said: "In applying the law one must match the crime: for one part of guilt give one part of punishment, for ten parts of guilt give ten parts of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Agui said: "In applying the law one must match the crime: for one part of guilt give one part of punishment, for ten parts of guilt give ten parts of punishment.

sentences.zh: 」阿克敦怒，索杖，阿桂惶恐求教。

translations.literal: " Akedun grew angry and called for a staff; Agui, in fear, begged instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " Akedun grew angry and called for a staff; Agui, in fear, begged instruction.

sentences.zh: 阿克敦曰：「如汝言，天下無完人矣！

translations.literal: Akedun said: "By your reasoning there would be no whole man under heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Akedun said: "By your reasoning there would be no whole man under heaven!

sentences.zh: 罪十分，治之五六，已不能堪，而可盡耶？

translations.literal: When guilt is ten parts, to punish five or six is already more than one can bear—how could one punish it all?
translations.idiomatic: When guilt is ten parts, to punish five or six is already more than one can bear—how could one punish it all?

sentences.zh: 且一分罪尚足問耶？

translations.literal: And is even one part of guilt worth prosecuting?
translations.idiomatic: And is even one part of guilt worth prosecuting?

sentences.zh: 」阿桂長刑部，屢舉以告僚屬雲。

translations.literal: " When Agui headed the Ministry of Punishments he repeatedly cited this story to tell his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: " When Agui headed the Ministry of Punishments he repeatedly cited this story to tell his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 孫嘉淦，字錫公，山西興縣人。

translations.literal: Sun Jiagan, styled Xigong, was a native of Xing County in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiagan (courtesy name Xigong) was from Xing County, Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉淦故家貧，耕且讀。

translations.literal: Jiagan's family had long been poor; he farmed while he studied.
translations.idiomatic: Jiagan's family had long been poor; he farmed while he studied.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年，成進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 52 he passed the jinshi examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 世宗初即位，命諸臣皆得上封事。

translations.literal: When Yongzheng had just acceded, he ordered that all officials might submit sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongzheng had just acceded, he ordered that all officials might submit sealed memorials.

sentences.zh: 嘉淦上疏陳三事：請親骨肉，停捐納，罷西兵。

translations.literal: Jiagan memorialized setting forth three matters: asking that imperial kin be treated with affection, that the sale of offices be halted, and that western troops be disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: Jiagan memorialized on three matters: asking that imperial kin be treated with affection, that the sale of offices be halted, and that western troops be disbanded.

sentences.zh: 上召諸大臣示之，且曰：「翰林院乃容此狂生耶？

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the ministers and showed it to them, saying: "Does the Hanlin Academy harbor such a wild youth?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the ministers and showed it to them, saying: "Does the Hanlin Academy harbor such a wild youth?

sentences.zh: 」大學士硃軾侍，徐對曰：「嘉淦誠狂，然臣服其膽。

translations.literal: " Grand Secretary Zhu Shi attended and answered slowly: "Jiagan is indeed wild, yet your servant admires his courage.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Secretary Zhu Shi attended and answered slowly: "Jiagan is indeed wild, yet your servant admires his courage.

sentences.zh: 」上良久笑曰：「朕亦且服其膽。

translations.literal: " After a long pause the emperor smiled and said: "I too must admire his courage.
translations.idiomatic: " After a long pause the emperor smiled and said: "I too must admire his courage.

sentences.zh: 」擢國子監司業。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，遷祭酒，命在南書房行走。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Academy and ordered to serve in the Southern Studio.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 4 he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Academy and ordered to serve in the Southern Studio.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，署順天府府尹。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year he acted as Prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 6 he served as acting Prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服未闋，召還京，仍授府尹。

translations.literal: On his father's death he entered mourning; before mourning was complete he was recalled to the capital and again appointed Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he entered mourning; before mourning was complete he was recalled to the capital and again appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 進工部侍郎，仍兼府尹、祭酒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Works while still holding concurrently the posts of Prefect and Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Works while still serving concurrently as prefect and director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 十年，調刑部侍郎，尋兼署吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments and soon after also acted as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments and soon after also served as acting Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嘉淦為祭酒，薦其弟揚淦為國子監丞。

translations.literal: While Jiagan was Director of the Imperial Academy he recommended his younger brother Yanggan as Assistant Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: While Jiagan was director of the Imperial Academy he recommended his younger brother Yanggan as assistant director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 教習宋鎬、方從仁等期滿引見，嘉淦言鎬等皆可用；

translations.literal: When the instructors Song Hao, Fang Congren, and others completed their term and were presented for audience, Jiagan said Hao and the others were all usable;
translations.idiomatic: When the instructors Song Hao, Fang Congren, and others completed their term and were presented for audience, Jiagan said Hao and the others were all usable;

sentences.zh: 上詰之，又言從仁實不堪用。

translations.literal: the emperor questioned him, and he then said Congren was in fact unfit for use.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor questioned him, and he then said Congren was in fact unfit for use.

sentences.zh: 上乃大怒，斥嘉淦反覆欺罔，奪職，交刑部治罪，當挾詐欺公律擬斬。

translations.literal: The emperor then grew greatly angry, rebuked Jiagan for shifting and deceitful conduct, stripped him of office, and handed him to the Ministry of Punishments for punishment; under the statute on fraud and deception of the public, death was recommended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then grew greatly angry, rebuked Jiagan for shifting and deceitful conduct, stripped him of office, and handed him to the Ministry of Punishments for punishment; under the statute on fraud and deception of the public, death was recommended.

sentences.zh: 上語諸大臣曰：「孫嘉淦太戇，然不愛錢。

translations.literal: The emperor told the ministers: "Sun Jiagan is too blunt, yet he does not love money.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the ministers: "Sun Jiagan is too blunt, yet he does not love money.

sentences.zh: 」命免罪，在戶部銀庫效力行走。

translations.literal: " He ordered the punishment waived and that Jiagan serve in the Ministry of Revenue's silver vault.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the punishment waived and that Jiagan serve in the Ministry of Revenue's silver vault.

sentences.zh: 嘉淦出獄，徑詣庫。

translations.literal: Jiagan left prison and went straight to the vault.
translations.idiomatic: Jiagan left prison and went straight to the vault.

sentences.zh: 果親王允禮時領戶部，疑嘉淦故大臣，被黜，不屑會計事；

translations.literal: Prince Guo Yunli then headed the Ministry of Revenue and suspected that Jiagan, a former high minister now disgraced, would disdain accounting work;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guo Yunli then headed the Ministry of Revenue and suspected that Jiagan, a former high minister now disgraced, would disdain accounting work;

sentences.zh: 又聞蜚語謂嘉淦沽名，收銀皆不足。

translations.literal: he also heard gossip saying Jiagan sought a reputation and that the silver he received was always short.
translations.idiomatic: he also heard gossip saying Jiagan sought a reputation and that the silver he received was always short.

sentences.zh: 乃蒞視，嘉淦方持衡稱量，與吏卒雜坐均勞苦。

translations.literal: He therefore went to inspect; Jiagan was just then holding the scales and weighing, sitting mixed among clerks and runners and sharing their labor.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore went to inspect; Jiagan was just then holding the scales and weighing, sitting mixed among clerks and runners and sharing their labor.

sentences.zh: 詢所收銀，則別置一所，覆之，無絲毫贏絀。

translations.literal: Asked about the silver received, it was set apart in a separate place, covered over, with not the slightest surplus or shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the silver received, it was set apart in a separate place, covered over, with not the slightest surplus or shortage.

sentences.zh: 事上聞，上愈重嘉淦。

translations.literal: The matter was reported to the emperor, and he valued Jiagan all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was reported to the emperor, and he valued Jiagan all the more.

sentences.zh: 十二年，命署河東鹽政。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was ordered to act as Salt Controller of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was ordered to serve as acting Salt Controller of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 十三年八月，高宗即位，召嘉淦來京，以侍郎候補。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year, when the Qianlong Emperor acceded, Jiagan was summoned to the capital to await appointment as a vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 13, when Qianlong acceded, Jiagan was summoned to the capital to await appointment as a vice minister.

sentences.zh: 九月，授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遷都察院左都御史，仍兼吏部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief of the Left in the Censorate while still holding the Ministry of Personnel concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief while still holding the Ministry of Personnel concurrently.

sentences.zh: 嘉淦以上初政，春秋方盛，上疏言：「臣本至愚，荷蒙皇上聖恩，畀以風紀重任。

translations.literal: Because the emperor's rule was just beginning and he was in the prime of life, Jiagan memorialized: "Your servant is by nature most dull, yet I have received Your Majesty's sacred grace and been entrusted with the weighty charge of discipline and oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor's rule was just beginning and he was in the prime of life, Jiagan memorialized: "Your servant is by nature most dull, yet I have received Your Majesty's sacred grace and been entrusted with the weighty charge of discipline and oversight.

sentences.zh: 日夜悚惶，思竭一得之慮；

translations.literal: Day and night I am fearful and anxious, thinking to exhaust whatever trifling counsel I may offer;
translations.idiomatic: Day and night I am fearful and anxious, thinking to exhaust whatever trifling counsel I may offer;

sentences.zh: 而每月以來，捧讀聖訓，剴切周詳，仁政固已舉行，臣愚更無可言。

translations.literal: yet month after month, reverently reading the sacred instructions, I find them earnest, thorough, and complete; benevolent policies are already being carried out, and this dull servant has nothing further to say.
translations.idiomatic: yet month after month, reverently reading the sacred instructions, I find them earnest, thorough, and complete; benevolent policies are already being carried out, and this dull servant has nothing further to say.

sentences.zh: 所欲言者，皇上之心而已。

translations.literal: What I wish to speak of is none other than Your Majesty's heart.
translations.idiomatic: What I wish to speak of is none other than Your Majesty's heart.

sentences.zh: 皇上之心，仁孝誠敬，明恕精一，豈復尚有可議？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heart is benevolent, filial, sincere, reverent, clear-sighted, forgiving, and single-minded—what could still be open to question?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's heart is benevolent, filial, sincere, reverent, clear-sighted, forgiving, and single-minded—what could still be open to question?

sentences.zh: 而臣猶欲有言者，正於心無不純、政無不善之中，竊鰓鰓私憂過計而欲預防之也。

translations.literal: Yet I still wish to speak, precisely because amid a heart without impurity and policies without fault I privately harbor anxious, perhaps excessive worry and wish to guard against what may come.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I still wish to speak, precisely because amid a heart without impurity and policies without fault I privately harbor anxious, perhaps excessive worry and wish to guard against what may come.

sentences.zh: 治亂之循環，如陰陽之運行。

translations.literal: The cycle of order and disorder is like the movement of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: The cycle of order and disorder is like the movement of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 陰極盛而陽生，陽極盛而陰姤。

translations.literal: When yin reaches its fullness yang is born; when yang reaches its fullness yin encounters it.
translations.idiomatic: When yin reaches its fullness yang is born; when yang reaches its fullness yin encounters it.

sentences.zh: 事當極盛之地，必有陰伏之機。

translations.literal: When affairs stand at the height of prosperity, the hidden workings of yin must already be present.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs stand at the height of prosperity, the hidden workings of decline must already be present.

sentences.zh: 其機藏於至微，人不能覺；

translations.literal: Its mechanism lies hidden in the subtlest depths, and people cannot perceive it;
translations.idiomatic: Its mechanism lies hidden in the subtlest depths, beyond anyone's notice;

sentences.zh: 及其既著，積重而不可返。

translations.literal: once it has become manifest, it accumulates weight and cannot be reversed.
translations.idiomatic: but once it has become manifest, the weight accumulates until there is no turning back.

sentences.zh: 此其間有三習焉，不可不慎戒也。

translations.literal: Within this interval there are three habits—one must not fail to guard against them with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: In this interval lie three habits against which one must guard with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 主德清則臣心服而頌，仁政行則民身受而感，出一言而盈廷稱聖，發一令而四海謳歌，在臣民本非獻諛，然而人主之耳則熟於此矣。

translations.literal: When the ruler's virtue is pure, ministers' hearts submit and they offer praise; when benevolent policies are carried out, the people feel them in their own persons and are moved. A single word spoken fills the court with cries of 'sage,' a single order issued brings songs of praise from all within the four seas. Among ministers and people this is not originally flattery offered up, yet the ruler's ears grow accustomed to this.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler's virtue is pure, ministers submit and praise him; when benevolent policies take effect, the people feel them and are moved. One word fills the court with cries of 'sage'; one order brings songs of praise from all the realm. Ministers and commoners may not mean this as flattery, yet the ruler's ears grow accustomed to it.

sentences.zh: 耳與譽化，非譽則逆，始而匡拂者拒，繼而木訥者厭，久而頌揚之不工者亦絀矣。

translations.literal: The ears merge with praise—what is not praise is taken as opposition. At first those who remonstrate and correct are rejected; next the slow of speech and dull of wit are disliked; in time even those whose praise and flattery are unskilled are dismissed as inadequate.
translations.idiomatic: The ears merge with praise—anything that is not praise is taken as opposition. At first remonstrators are rejected; then the slow-tongued and dull-witted are disliked; in time even those whose praise is clumsy are dismissed.

sentences.zh: 是謂耳習於所聞，則喜諛而惡直。

translations.literal: This is what is called the ear growing habituated to what it hears, so that one delights in flattery and hates forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: This is the habit of the ear: growing accustomed to what it hears until one delights in flattery and hates forthrightness.

sentences.zh: 上愈智則下愈愚，上愈能則下愈畏，趨蹌諂脅，顧盻而皆然，免冠叩首，應聲而即是。

translations.literal: The more intelligent the ruler above, the more foolish those below; the more capable the ruler above, the more fearful those below. Scurrying, fawning, and cringing—all turn their glances and act the same; doffing caps and kowtowing, they assent the moment a word is spoken.
translations.idiomatic: The more intelligent the ruler, the more foolish his subordinates appear; the more capable the ruler, the more fearful they become. All scurry, fawn, and cringe alike; caps are doffed and heads bowed the instant a word is spoken.

sentences.zh: 此在臣工以為盡禮，然而人主之目則熟於此矣。

translations.literal: Among officials this is regarded as the full observance of ritual propriety, yet the ruler's eyes grow accustomed to this.
translations.idiomatic: Officials may regard this as perfect propriety, yet the ruler's eyes grow accustomed to it.

sentences.zh: 目與媚化，非媚則觸，故始而倨野者斥，繼而嚴憚者疏，久而便闢之不巧者亦忤矣。

translations.literal: The eyes merge with obsequiousness—what is not obsequious gives offense. Hence at first the arrogant and boorish are expelled; next the solemn and cautious are kept at a distance; in time even those whose agility and glibness are clumsy also give offense.
translations.idiomatic: The eyes merge with obsequiousness—anything that is not obsequious gives offense. At first the arrogant and boorish are expelled; then the solemn and cautious are kept at a distance; in time even the clumsily glib give offense.

sentences.zh: 是謂目習於所見，則喜柔而惡剛。

translations.literal: This is what is called the eye growing habituated to what it sees, so that one delights in softness and hates firmness.
translations.idiomatic: This is the habit of the eye: growing accustomed to what it sees until one delights in softness and hates firmness.

sentences.zh: 敬求天下之事，見之多而以為無足奇也，則高己而卑人；

translations.literal: Diligently inquiring into affairs throughout the realm, one sees so much that nothing seems remarkable, and then one exalts oneself and looks down on others;
translations.idiomatic: Diligently inquiring into affairs throughout the realm, one sees so much that nothing seems remarkable—and so one exalts oneself and looks down on others;

sentences.zh: 慎辨天下之務，閱之久而以為無難也，則雄才而易事；

translations.literal: carefully distinguishing the business of the realm, one examines it for so long that nothing seems difficult, and then one deems oneself heroic in talent and treats affairs lightly;
translations.idiomatic: carefully distinguishing the business of the realm, one examines it so long that nothing seems difficult—and so one deems oneself heroically talented and treats affairs lightly;

sentences.zh: 質之人而不聞其所短，返之己而不見其所失。

translations.literal: questioning others yet never hearing of one's own shortcomings, turning back to oneself yet never seeing one's own errors.
translations.idiomatic: questioning others yet never hearing of one's own shortcomings, turning inward yet never seeing one's own errors.

sentences.zh: 於是乎意之所欲，信以為不逾，令之所發，概期於必行矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon whatever the mind desires is trusted as not exceeding bounds, and whatever orders are issued are altogether expected to be carried out without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon whatever the mind desires is trusted as beyond reproach, and every order issued is expected to be carried out without fail.

sentences.zh: 是謂心習於所是，則喜從而惡違。

translations.literal: This is what is called the heart growing habituated to what it approves, so that one delights in compliance and hates opposition.
translations.idiomatic: This is the habit of the heart: growing accustomed to what it approves until one delights in compliance and hates opposition.

sentences.zh: 三習既成，乃生一弊。

translations.literal: Once the three habits have taken shape, a single defect is born.
translations.idiomatic: Once the three habits have taken shape, a single defect arises.

sentences.zh: 何謂一弊？

translations.literal: What is this single defect?
translations.idiomatic: What is this single defect?

sentences.zh: 喜小人而厭君子是也。

translations.literal: It is to delight in petty men and dislike gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: It is to delight in petty men and dislike gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 今夫進君子而退小人，豈獨三代以上知之哉？

translations.literal: As for advancing gentlemen and dismissing petty men—is this knowledge possessed only by those above the Three Dynasties?
translations.idiomatic: As for advancing gentlemen and dismissing petty men—is this wisdom known only to the sages of antiquity?

sentences.zh: 雖叔季之君，孰不思用君子？

translations.literal: Even rulers of declining ages—who among them did not wish to employ gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: Even rulers of declining ages—who among them did not wish to employ gentlemen?

sentences.zh: 且自智之君，各賢其臣，孰不以為吾所用者必君子而決非小人？

translations.literal: Moreover, self-assured intelligent rulers each deem their ministers worthy—who among them did not believe that those they employed must be gentlemen and certainly not petty men?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, self-assured intelligent rulers each deem their ministers worthy—who among them did not believe that those they employed must be gentlemen and certainly not petty men?

sentences.zh: 乃卒之小人進而君子退者，無他，用才而不用德故也。

translations.literal: Yet in the end petty men advance and gentlemen withdraw—there is no other reason: it is because talent is used and virtue is not.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end petty men advance and gentlemen withdraw—for no other reason than that talent is valued and virtue is not.

sentences.zh: 德者君子之所獨，才則君子小人共之，而且小人勝焉。

translations.literal: Virtue belongs to gentlemen alone; talent is shared by gentlemen and petty men alike, and among them petty men excel.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue belongs to gentlemen alone; talent is shared by gentlemen and petty men alike—and petty men excel at it.

sentences.zh: 語言奏對，君子訥而小人佞諛，則與耳習投矣。

translations.literal: In speech and audience, gentlemen are blunt while petty men are glib and flattering—this aligns with the habit of the ear.
translations.idiomatic: In speech and audience, gentlemen are blunt while petty men are glib and flattering—this suits the habit of the ear.

sentences.zh: 奔走周旋，君子拙而小人便闢，則與目習投矣。

translations.literal: In rushing about and attending upon the ruler, gentlemen are awkward while petty men are agile and glib—this aligns with the habit of the eye.
translations.idiomatic: In rushing about and attending upon the ruler, gentlemen are awkward while petty men are agile and glib—this suits the habit of the eye.

sentences.zh: 即課事考勞，君子孤行其意而恥於言功，小人巧於迎合而工於顯勤，則與心習又投矣。

translations.literal: Even in assessing affairs and examining merit, gentlemen pursue their own intent in solitude and are ashamed to speak of their achievements, while petty men are clever at accommodating and skilled at displaying diligence—this again aligns with the habit of the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Even in assessing affairs and examining merit, gentlemen pursue their own intent in solitude and are ashamed to speak of their achievements, while petty men are clever at accommodating and skilled at displaying diligence—this again suits the habit of the heart.

sentences.zh: 小人挾其所長以善投，人主溺於所習而不覺，審聽之而其言入耳，諦觀之而其顏悅目，歷試之而其才稱乎心也，於是乎小人不約而自合，君子不逐而自離。

translations.literal: Petty men wield their strengths to fit well; the ruler, drowning in what he has grown accustomed to, is unaware. Listen carefully and their words enter the ear pleasantly; look closely and their countenances please the eye; test them repeatedly and their talents satisfy the heart—whereupon petty men unite without being summoned, and gentlemen depart without being driven away.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men wield their strengths to fit perfectly; the ruler, drowning in habit, notices nothing. Listen carefully and their words please the ear; look closely and their faces please the eye; test them and their talents satisfy the heart—whereupon petty men gather without being summoned and gentlemen withdraw without being driven away.

sentences.zh: 夫至於小人合而君子離，其患可勝言哉？

translations.literal: When it comes to petty men gathering and gentlemen departing, can the harm be fully expressed in words?
translations.idiomatic: When petty men gather and gentlemen depart, can the harm even be put into words?

sentences.zh: 而揆厥所由，皆三習為之蔽焉。

translations.literal: Yet tracing the source of it all, the three habits are what obscure the ruler's judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet tracing the source of it all, the three habits are what obscure the ruler's judgment.

sentences.zh: 治亂之機，千古一轍，可考而知也。

translations.literal: The mechanism of order and disorder follows the same track throughout the ages—it can be examined and understood.
translations.idiomatic: The mechanism of order and disorder follows the same track throughout the ages—it can be examined and understood.

sentences.zh: 我皇上聖明臨御，如日中天，豈惟並無此弊，抑且並無此習。

translations.literal: Our emperor, sage and enlightened upon the throne, is like the sun at its zenith—how could he not only be free of this defect but also free of these habits?
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor, sage and enlightened upon the throne, is like the sun at its zenith—not only free of this defect but free of these habits as well.

sentences.zh: 然臣正及其未習也而言之，設其習既成，則或有知之而不敢言，抑或言之而不見聽者矣。

translations.literal: Yet your servant speaks precisely while these habits have not yet formed. Suppose they have already taken shape—then some who know may not dare to speak, or if they speak they may not be heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your servant speaks precisely while these habits have not yet formed. Once they have taken shape, some who know may not dare to speak—or if they speak, they may not be heeded.

sentences.zh: 今欲預除三習，永杜一弊，不在乎外，惟在乎心，故臣原言皇上之心也。

translations.literal: Now to forestall the three habits in advance and forever shut out the one defect—this lies not in externals but solely in the heart. Hence your servant wishes to speak of Your Majesty's heart.
translations.idiomatic: To forestall the three habits in advance and forever shut out the one defect lies not in externals but solely in the heart. Hence your servant wishes to speak of Your Majesty's heart.

sentences.zh: 語曰：'人非聖人，孰能無過？

translations.literal: The saying goes: 'If one is not a sage, who can be without fault?
translations.idiomatic: The saying goes: 'If one is not a sage, who can be without fault?

sentences.zh: '此淺言也。

translations.literal: ' This is shallow talk.
translations.idiomatic: ' This is shallow talk.

sentences.zh: 夫聖人豈無過哉？

translations.literal: Do sages truly have no faults?
translations.idiomatic: Do sages truly have no faults?

sentences.zh: 惟聖人而後能知過，惟聖人而後能改過。

translations.literal: Only after one is a sage can one recognize one's faults; only after one is a sage can one amend one's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Only a sage can recognize his faults; only a sage can amend them.

sentences.zh: 孔子謂五十學易，可無大過。

translations.literal: Confucius said that at fifty, having studied the Changes, one might be free of great faults.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said that at fifty, having studied the Changes, one might be free of great faults.

sentences.zh: 文王視民如傷，望道如未之見。

translations.literal: King Wen regarded the people as though they were wounded, and gazed upon the Way as though he had not yet seen it.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen regarded the people as though they were wounded, and gazed upon the Way as though he had not yet seen it.

sentences.zh: 是故賢人之過，賢人知之，庸人不知也。

translations.literal: Therefore the faults of the worthy are known to the worthy; ordinary men do not know them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the faults of the worthy are known to the worthy; ordinary men do not know them.

sentences.zh: 聖人之過，聖人知之，賢人不知也。

translations.literal: The faults of sages are known to sages; the worthy do not know them.
translations.idiomatic: The faults of sages are known to sages; the worthy do not know them.

sentences.zh: 慾望人繩愆糾謬而及於其所不知，難已。

translations.literal: To expect others to correct errors and rectify mistakes in matters one does not oneself perceive—this is difficult indeed.
translations.idiomatic: To expect others to correct errors and rectify mistakes in matters one does not oneself perceive—this is difficult indeed.

sentences.zh: 故望皇上聖心自懍之也。

translations.literal: Hence your servant hopes that Your Majesty's sage heart will be vigilant of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Hence your servant hopes that Your Majesty's sage heart will be vigilant of itself.

sentences.zh: 反之己真知其不足，驗之世實見其未能，故常欿然不敢自是。

translations.literal: Turning back upon oneself, truly knowing one's insufficiency; testing oneself against the world, truly seeing one's inadequacy—thus one is constantly uneasy and dares not be self-satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Turning inward, truly knowing one's insufficiency; testing oneself against the world, truly seeing one's inadequacy—thus one is constantly uneasy and dares not be self-satisfied.

sentences.zh: 此不敢自是之意，流貫於用人行政之間，夫而後知諫爭切磋，愛我良深，而諛悅為容者，愚己而陷之阱也；

translations.literal: This spirit of not daring to be self-satisfied flows through the employment of men and the conduct of government—only then does one know that remonstrance and earnest counsel love one deeply, while those who flatter and please to win favor are traps that delude oneself and lead one into ruin;
translations.idiomatic: This spirit of not daring to be self-satisfied flows through the employment of men and the conduct of government—only then does one know that remonstrance and earnest counsel love one deeply, while those who flatter to win favor are traps that delude oneself and lead one into ruin;

sentences.zh: 夫而後知嚴憚匡拂，益我良多，而順從不違者，推己而墜之淵也。

translations.literal: only then does one know that solemn caution and corrective remonstrance benefit one greatly, while those who comply without dissent are abysses into which one pushes oneself and falls.
translations.idiomatic: only then does one know that solemn caution and corrective remonstrance benefit one greatly, while those who comply without dissent are abysses into which one pushes oneself and falls.

sentences.zh: 耳目之習除，取捨之極定，夫而後眾正盈朝，太平可睹矣。

translations.literal: When the habits of ear and eye are removed and the standards of selection and rejection are firmly set—only then will the upright fill the court and great peace be within sight.
translations.idiomatic: When the habits of ear and eye are removed and the standards of selection and rejection are firmly set, the upright will fill the court and great peace will be within sight.

sentences.zh: 不然，自是之根不拔，則雖斂心為慎，慎之久而覺其無過，則謂可以少寬；

translations.literal: Otherwise, if the root of self-satisfaction is not uprooted, then though one restrains the heart in caution, after long caution one feels oneself without fault and thinks one may relax a little;
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, if the root of self-satisfaction is not uprooted, then though one restrains the heart in caution, after long caution one feels oneself without fault and thinks one may relax a little;

sentences.zh: 厲志為勤，勤之久而覺其有功，則謂可以少慰。

translations.literal: though one sharpens the will in diligence, after long diligence one feels oneself has achieved merit and thinks one may take a little comfort.
translations.idiomatic: though one sharpens the will in diligence, after long diligence one feels oneself has achieved merit and thinks one may take a little comfort.

sentences.zh: 此念一轉，初亦似於天下無害，而不知嗜欲燕安功利之說，漸入耳而不煩，而便闢善柔便佞者，亦熟視而不見其可憎。

translations.literal: Once this thought turns, at first it seems harmless to the realm—yet unawares, talk of indulgence, ease, comfort, and profit gradually enters the ear without annoyance, and the agile, soft, and glib flatterers are also looked upon so long that their hatefulness is no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: Once this thought turns, at first it seems harmless to the realm—yet unawares, talk of indulgence, ease, and profit gradually enters the ear without annoyance, and the agile, soft, glib flatterers are looked upon so long that their hatefulness is no longer seen.

sentences.zh: 久而習焉，或不自知而為其所中，則黑白可以轉色，而東西可以易位。

translations.literal: Over time one grows habituated; perhaps without knowing it one is struck by them—then black and white can change color, and east and west can exchange places.
translations.idiomatic: Over time one grows habituated; perhaps without knowing it one is struck by them—then black and white can change color, and east and west can exchange places.

sentences.zh: 所謂機伏於至微而勢成於不可返者，此之謂也。

translations.literal: What is called the mechanism lying hidden in the subtlest depths while the momentum forms until it cannot be reversed—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by the mechanism lying hidden in the subtlest depths while momentum forms until there is no turning back.

sentences.zh: 大學言'見賢而不能舉，見不賢而不能退'，至於好惡拂人之性；

translations.literal: The Great Learning says, 'Seeing the worthy yet unable to elevate them, seeing the unworthy yet unable to dismiss them'—so that likes and dislikes run counter to human nature;
translations.idiomatic: The Great Learning says, 'Seeing the worthy yet unable to elevate them, seeing the unworthy yet unable to dismiss them'—so that likes and dislikes run counter to human nature;

sentences.zh: 而推所由失，皆因於驕泰，驕泰即自是之謂也。

translations.literal: and tracing the source of failure, it all stems from arrogance and complacency—arrogance and complacency are what self-satisfaction means.
translations.idiomatic: and tracing the source of failure, it all stems from arrogance and complacency—arrogance and complacency are self-satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，治亂之機，轉於君子小人之進退；

translations.literal: Viewed from this perspective, the mechanism of order and disorder turns upon the advance and withdrawal of gentlemen and petty men;
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from this perspective, the mechanism of order and disorder turns upon the advance and withdrawal of gentlemen and petty men;

sentences.zh: 進退之機，握於人主之一心；

translations.literal: the mechanism of advance and withdrawal is held in the single heart of the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: the mechanism of advance and withdrawal is held in the single heart of the ruler;

sentences.zh: 能知非則心不期敬而自敬，不見過則心不期肆而自肆。

translations.literal: One who can recognize error—though the heart does not expect reverence, it becomes reverent of itself; one who does not see faults—though the heart does not expect license, it becomes licentious of itself.
translations.idiomatic: One who can recognize error becomes reverent without intending it; one who does not see faults becomes licentious without intending it.

sentences.zh: 敬者君子之招而治之本也，肆者小人之媒而亂之階也。

translations.literal: Reverence summons gentlemen and is the root of order; license is the medium of petty men and the stairway to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Reverence summons gentlemen and is the root of order; license is the medium of petty men and the stairway to disorder.

sentences.zh: 然則沿流溯源，約言蔽義，惟望我皇上時時事事常守此不敢自是之心，而天德王道舉不外乎此矣。

translations.literal: Thus tracing upstream to the source and summing up the meaning in brief words, your servant only hopes that our emperor, in every moment and every affair, will constantly keep this heart that dares not be self-satisfied—and then the virtue of Heaven and the kingly Way will all lie within this and nothing beyond it.
translations.idiomatic: Thus tracing upstream to the source and summing up the meaning in brief, your servant only hopes that our emperor, in every moment and every affair, will constantly keep this heart that dares not be self-satisfied—for the virtue of Heaven and the kingly Way lie in nothing beyond this.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，上嘉納，宣示。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted; the emperor commended and accepted it and had it promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted; the emperor commended and accepted it and had it promulgated.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，總理國子監事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice and given overall charge of affairs at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Justice and given overall charge of affairs at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 河南鄭州有疑獄，命使者往勘，仍不得實。

translations.literal: In Zhengzhou, Henan, there was a doubtful legal case; envoys were sent to investigate, yet the truth could still not be established.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengzhou, Henan, there was a doubtful legal case; envoys were sent to investigate, yet the truth could still not be established.

sentences.zh: 上命嘉淦往訊，得其冤狀十餘人盡脫之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jiagan to go and examine the case; he found the circumstances of wrongful conviction, and more than ten persons were entirely exonerated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jiagan to go and examine the case; he found the circumstances of wrongful conviction, and more than ten persons were entirely exonerated.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年四月，遷吏部尚書，仍兼管刑部事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of the Qianlong reign, he was transferred to Minister of Personnel while still retaining concurrent charge of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of the Qianlong reign, he was transferred to Minister of Personnel while still retaining concurrent charge of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 九月，直隸總督李衛劾總河硃藻貪劣誤工，命偕尚書訥親往鞫，得實，論如律。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Li Wei, Governor-General of Zhili, impeached Zhu Zao, Director-General of River Conservancy, for corruption, incompetence, and dereliction of duty. Jiagan was ordered to go jointly with Minister Neqin to try the case; the charges were substantiated and judgment was passed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Li Wei, Governor-General of Zhili, impeached Zhu Zao, Director-General of River Conservancy, for corruption, incompetence, and dereliction of duty. Jiagan was ordered to go jointly with Minister Neqin to try the case; the charges were substantiated and judgment was passed according to law.

sentences.zh: 十月，授直隸總督。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he was appointed Governor-General of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, he was appointed Governor-General of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 時畿輔酒禁甚嚴，罹法者眾。

translations.literal: At the time the prohibition on wine in the capital region was very strict, and those who violated the law were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the prohibition on wine in the capital region was very strict, and violators were numerous.

sentences.zh: 嘉淦疏言：「前督李衛任內，一年中獲私釀三百六十四案，犯者千四百餘名。

translations.literal: Jiagan memorialized: "During the tenure of the previous governor Li Wei, in one year three hundred and sixty-four cases of illicit brewing were seized, involving more than fourteen hundred offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Jiagan memorialized: "During the tenure of the previous governor Li Wei, in one year three hundred and sixty-four cases of illicit brewing were seized, involving more than fourteen hundred offenders.

sentences.zh: 臣抵任一月，獲私釀七十八案，犯者三百五十餘名。

translations.literal: Within one month of your servant's arrival in office, seventy-eight cases of illicit brewing were seized, involving more than three hundred and fifty offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Within one month of your servant's arrival in office, seventy-eight cases of illicit brewing were seized, involving more than three hundred and fifty offenders.

sentences.zh: 此特申報者耳，府、廳、州、縣自結之案，尚復不知凡幾。

translations.literal: These are only the cases formally reported; as for cases concluded on their own authority by prefectures, subprefectures, departments, and counties, one cannot know how many more there are.
translations.idiomatic: These are only the cases formally reported; as for cases concluded on their own authority by prefectures, subprefectures, departments, and counties, one cannot know how many more there are.

sentences.zh: 吏役兵丁已獲而賄縱者，更不知凡幾。

translations.literal: As for clerks, runners, and soldiers who were caught yet released after taking bribes, one cannot know how many more there are.
translations.idiomatic: As for clerks, runners, and soldiers who were caught yet released after taking bribes, one cannot know how many more there are.

sentences.zh: 此特犯者之正身耳，其鄉保鄰甲、沿途店肆、負販之屬牽連受累者，又復不知凡幾。

translations.literal: These are only the principal offenders themselves; as for village heads, neighborhood wardens, shops along the roads, peddlers, and others implicated and harmed by association, one cannot know how many more there are.
translations.idiomatic: These are only the principal offenders themselves; as for village heads, neighborhood wardens, roadside shops, peddlers, and others implicated and harmed by association, one cannot know how many more there are.

sentences.zh: 一省如是，他省可知。

translations.literal: If one province is thus, the other provinces may be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: If one province is thus, the other provinces may be inferred.

sentences.zh: 皇上好生卹刑，命盜案自罹重闢，尚再三酌議，求一線可原之路。

translations.literal: Your Majesty cherishes life and shows compassion in punishment—even in robbery cases where the penalty of dismemberment applies, you still deliberate repeatedly, seeking some thread of grounds for clemency.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty cherishes life and shows compassion in punishment—even in robbery cases where the penalty of dismemberment applies, you still deliberate repeatedly, seeking some thread of grounds for clemency.

sentences.zh: 今以日用飲食之故，官吏兵役以私釀為利藪，百姓弱者失業，強者犯令，鹽梟未靖，酒梟復起，天下騷然，殊非政體。

translations.literal: Now on account of daily food and drink, officials, clerks, and soldiers treat illicit brewing as a source of profit; among the common people the weak lose their livelihood and the strong violate the prohibition. Salt smugglers have not yet been pacified, and wine smugglers rise again—the realm is in turmoil; this is utterly contrary to proper governance.
translations.idiomatic: Now on account of daily food and drink, officials, clerks, and soldiers treat illicit brewing as a source of profit; among the common people the weak lose their livelihood and the strong violate the prohibition. Salt smugglers have not yet been pacified, and wine smugglers rise again—the realm is in turmoil; this is utterly contrary to proper governance.

sentences.zh: 臣前言酒禁宜於歉歲，不宜於豐年，猶屬書生謬論。

translations.literal: Your servant's earlier statement that the wine prohibition is suitable in lean years but not in abundant years was still the mistaken argument of a bookish scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's earlier statement that the wine prohibition is suitable in lean years but not in abundant years was still the mistaken argument of a bookish scholar.

sentences.zh: 躬蒞其事，乃知奪民之貲財而狼藉之，毀民之肌膚而敲撲之，取民之生計而禁錮之。

translations.literal: Only upon personally overseeing the matter did I know that the people's property is seized and scattered in ruin, their flesh is battered and beaten, and their livelihoods are taken and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Only upon personally overseeing the matter did I know that the people's property is seized and scattered in ruin, their flesh is battered and beaten, and their livelihoods are taken and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 饑饉之餘，民無固志，失業既重，何事不為？

translations.literal: In the aftermath of famine, the people have no settled resolve; once livelihood is lost on so great a scale, what will they not do?
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of famine, the people have no settled resolve; once livelihood is lost on so great a scale, what will they not do?

sentences.zh: 歉歲之不可禁，乃更甚於豐穰。

translations.literal: That wine cannot be prohibited in lean years is even more true than in years of abundance.
translations.idiomatic: That wine cannot be prohibited in lean years is even more true than in years of abundance.

sentences.zh: 周禮荒政，舍禁去譏，有由然也。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou, in its famine policies, lifts market prohibitions and removes market inspectors—for good reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, in its famine policies, lifts market prohibitions and removes market inspectors—for good reason.

sentences.zh: 且也酒禁之行，無論適以擾民，而實終不能禁。

translations.literal: Moreover, the enforcement of the wine prohibition not only disturbs the people—it in fact cannot be permanently enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the enforcement of the wine prohibition not only disturbs the people—it in fact cannot be permanently enforced.

sentences.zh: 借令禁之不擾，且能永禁，而於貧民生計，米穀蓋藏，不惟無益，抑且有損。

translations.literal: Even supposing the prohibition did not disturb the people and could be permanently enforced, as regards the livelihood of the poor and the storage of grain, it would not only be without benefit but would actually cause harm.
translations.idiomatic: Even supposing the prohibition did not disturb the people and could be permanently enforced, as regards the livelihood of the poor and the storage of grain, it would not only be without benefit but would actually cause harm.

sentences.zh: 夫作酒以糜穀，此為黃酒言也，其麴必用小麥，其米則需睟稉，皆五穀之最精。

translations.literal: Now, making wine by consuming grain—this refers to yellow wine; its ferment must use wheat, and its rice requires polished glutinous grain—all the finest of the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Now, making wine by consuming grain—this refers to yellow wine; its ferment must use wheat, and its rice requires polished glutinous grain—all the finest of the five grains.

sentences.zh: 若燒酒則用高粱，佐以豆皮、黍殼、穀糠，麴以大麥為之，本非朝夕所食，而豆皮、黍殼、穀糠之屬，原屬棄物，雜而成酒，可以得價，其糟可飼六畜。

translations.literal: As for distilled liquor, it uses sorghum, supplemented by bean husks, millet chaff, and rice bran; the ferment is made from barley. These are not foods for daily consumption, while bean husks, millet chaff, rice bran, and the like are originally waste matter—mixed together they become wine and can fetch a price, and the dregs can feed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: As for distilled liquor, it uses sorghum, supplemented by bean husks, millet chaff, and rice bran; the ferment is made from barley. These are not foods for daily consumption, while bean husks, millet chaff, rice bran, and the like are originally waste matter—mixed together they become wine and can fetch a price, and the dregs can feed livestock.

sentences.zh: 化無用為有用，非作無益害有益也。

translations.literal: Transforming the useless into the useful—this is not doing what is harmful while destroying what is beneficial.
translations.idiomatic: Transforming the useless into the useful—this is not doing what is harmful while destroying what is beneficial.

sentences.zh: 今欲禁燒酒而並禁黃酒，則無以供祭祀、賓客、養老之用。

translations.literal: Now if one wishes to prohibit distilled liquor and also prohibit yellow wine, there will be none to supply sacrifices, guests, and the needs of the elderly.
translations.idiomatic: Now if one wishes to prohibit distilled liquor and also prohibit yellow wine, there will be none to supply sacrifices, guests, and the needs of the elderly.

sentences.zh: 若不禁黃酒止禁燒酒，省大麥、高梁之粗且賤者，而倍費小麥、睟稉之精且貴者，臣所謂無益於蓋藏也。

translations.literal: If yellow wine is not prohibited but only distilled liquor is, one saves the coarse and cheap barley and sorghum while doubling the expenditure of the fine and costly wheat and polished glutinous grain—this is what your servant means by no benefit to grain storage.
translations.idiomatic: If yellow wine is not prohibited but only distilled liquor is, one saves the coarse and cheap barley and sorghum while doubling the expenditure of the fine and costly wheat and polished glutinous grain—this is what your servant means by no benefit to grain storage.

sentences.zh: 百工所為，皆需易之以粟，太貴則病末，太賤則傷農，得其中而後農末俱利。

translations.literal: All the crafts require grain in exchange for their products; if grain is too costly the crafts suffer, if too cheap the farmers are harmed—only by hitting the mean can both farming and crafts profit.
translations.idiomatic: All the crafts require grain in exchange for their products; if grain is too costly the crafts suffer, if too cheap the farmers are harmed—only by hitting the mean can both farming and crafts profit.

sentences.zh: 故農有歉荒，亦有熟荒，十年以內，歉歲三而豐歲七，則粟宜有所洩，非但積之不用而已。

translations.literal: Thus in farming there are lean harvests and also harvests so abundant they become a hardship; within ten years, three are lean and seven are abundant—grain ought to have some outlet, not merely be stored unused.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in farming there are lean harvests and also harvests so abundant they become a hardship; within ten years, three are lean and seven are abundant—grain ought to have some outlet, not merely be stored unused.

sentences.zh: 今北地不種高粱，則無以為薪、席、屋牆之用，種之而用其稭稈，則其顆粒宜有所售。

translations.literal: Now in the northern regions, if sorghum is not planted, there is nothing for fuel, mats, and wall-building; if it is planted and the stalks are used, then the grain ought to have a market.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the northern regions, if sorghum is not planted, there is nothing for fuel, mats, and wall-building; if it is planted and the stalks are used, then the grain ought to have a market.

sentences.zh: 燒鍋既禁，富民不買高粱，貧民穫高粱，雖賤價而不售。

translations.literal: Once distilleries are prohibited, the wealthy no longer buy sorghum; the poor harvest sorghum yet even at low prices cannot sell it.
translations.idiomatic: Once distilleries are prohibited, the wealthy no longer buy sorghum; the poor harvest sorghum yet even at low prices cannot sell it.

sentences.zh: 高粱不售，而酒又為必需之物，則必賣米穀以買黃酒。

translations.literal: When sorghum cannot be sold and wine is still a daily necessity, they must sell rice and grain to buy yellow wine.
translations.idiomatic: When sorghum cannot be sold and wine is still a daily necessity, they must sell rice and grain to buy yellow wine.

sentences.zh: 向者一歲之內，八口之家，賣高粱之價，可得七八兩，今止二三兩矣；

translations.literal: Formerly, within one year, a household of eight persons could get seven or eight taels from selling sorghum; now it is only two or three taels;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, within one year, a household of eight persons could get seven or eight taels from selling sorghum; now it is only two or three taels;

sentences.zh: 而買黃酒之價，則需費七八兩。

translations.literal: yet the cost of buying yellow wine requires seven or eight taels.
translations.idiomatic: yet the cost of buying yellow wine requires seven or eight taels.

sentences.zh: 所入少而所出多，又加以粃糠等物堆積而不能易錢，自然之利皆失。

translations.literal: Income is little while outgo is great; moreover bran, chaff, and the like pile up and cannot be exchanged for cash—all natural advantages are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Income is little while outgo is great; moreover bran, chaff, and the like pile up and cannot be exchanged for cash—all natural advantages are lost.

sentences.zh: 日用所需，惟糶米麥。

translations.literal: For daily needs, they have only to sell off rice and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: For daily needs, they have only to sell off rice and wheat.

sentences.zh: 糶而售，則家無蓋藏；

translations.literal: If they sell and find buyers, the household has nothing stored away;
translations.idiomatic: If they sell and find buyers, the household has nothing stored away;

sentences.zh: 糶而不售，則百用皆絀。

translations.literal: if they sell yet cannot find buyers, then every need falls short.
translations.idiomatic: if they sell yet cannot find buyers, then every need falls short.

sentences.zh: 臣所謂有損於生計者此也。

translations.literal: This is what your servant means by harm to livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: This is what your servant means by harm to livelihood.

sentences.zh: 小民趨利，如水就下。

translations.literal: The common people pursue profit as water flows downward.
translations.idiomatic: The common people pursue profit as water flows downward.

sentences.zh: 利所不在，雖賞不為。

translations.literal: Where profit does not lie, even rewards will not move them.
translations.idiomatic: Where there is no profit, even rewards will not move people.

sentences.zh: 利之所在，雖禁彌甚。

translations.literal: Where profit lies, even severe prohibition grows all the stricter.
translations.idiomatic: Where profit lies, even the sternest prohibition only drives people harder.

sentences.zh: 燒鍋禁則酒必少，酒少則價必貴，價貴而私燒之利甚倍於昔。

translations.literal: If distilleries are banned, wine must become scarce; when wine is scarce prices must rise; when prices rise the profit from illicit distilling becomes many times greater than before.
translations.idiomatic: Ban distilleries and wine grows scarce; when wine is scarce, prices rise; when prices rise, illicit distilling yields many times the old profit.

sentences.zh: 什倍之利所在，民必性命爭焉。

translations.literal: Where profits are tenfold, the people will stake their lives competing for them.
translations.idiomatic: Where profits are tenfold, people will stake their lives to seize them.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰'君子不以所養人者害人'，本為民生計，而滋擾乃至此，則立法不可不慎也。

translations.literal: Mencius said, 'The gentleman does not harm people with what is used to nourish them.' The policy was meant for the people's livelihood, yet the disturbances reached this point—thus in making laws one cannot be inattentive.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, 'The gentleman does not harm people with what is meant to nourish them.' The measure was meant for the people's livelihood, yet the harassment reached this point—so in making laws one must be exceedingly careful.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，詔弛禁。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict relaxed the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, an edict relaxed the prohibition.

sentences.zh: 民王宰謀得諸生馬承宗產，賄太監劉金玉等投獻貝勒允祐門下，嘉淦疏請交刑部具讞，上嘉其能執法。

translations.literal: A commoner named Wang Zai plotted to seize the property of the licentiate Ma Chengzong, bribed the eunuchs Liu Jinyu and others, and presented it to Prince Yunyou's household. Jiagan memorialized requesting the Ministry of Punishments try the case and fix guilt; the Emperor praised his ability to uphold the law.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Wang Zai plotted to seize the property of the licentiate Ma Chengzong, bribed the eunuchs Liu Jinyu and others, and presented it to Prince Yunyou's household. Jiagan memorialized that the case be sent to the Ministry of Punishments for trial and judgment; the Emperor praised his firmness in upholding the law.

sentences.zh: 民焦韜被誣坐邪教，株連者數百人，嘉淦白其枉。

translations.literal: The commoner Jiao Tao was falsely charged with belonging to a heterodox sect; those implicated numbered in the hundreds. Jiagan cleared his wrongful conviction.
translations.idiomatic: The commoner Jiao Tao was falsely charged with belonging to a heterodox sect; hundreds were implicated. Jiagan cleared his wrongful conviction.

sentences.zh: 民紀懷讓食料豆汁染衣，會村有賊殺人，偵者以為血，誣服。

translations.literal: The commoner Ji Huairang had bean juice from his fodder stain his clothes; meanwhile a thief killed someone in the village, and investigators mistook the stain for blood, leading him to confess wrongly under torture.
translations.idiomatic: The commoner Ji Huairang had bean juice from his fodder stain his clothes; meanwhile a thief killed someone in the village, and investigators mistook the stain for blood, so he confessed under torture to a crime he did not commit.

sentences.zh: 決有日，正定知府陳浩廉得冤狀，嘉淦親鞫，雪懷讓。

translations.literal: The day of execution was set; the Zhengding prefect Chen Haolian obtained evidence of the injustice, and Jiagan personally tried the case and cleared Huairang.
translations.idiomatic: The day of execution was set; the Zhengding prefect Chen Haolian obtained evidence of the injustice, and Jiagan personally tried the case and cleared Huairang.

sentences.zh: 尋命兼管直隸河工，嘉淦議治永定河。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered also to oversee Zhili river works; Jiagan proposed regulating the Yongding River.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered also to oversee Zhili river works; Jiagan proposed regulating the Yongding River.

sentences.zh: 初至官，即請於金門閘上下多建草壩，使河流漸復故道。

translations.literal: Upon first assuming office, he asked to build many brush weirs above and below the Jinmen Sluice so the river might gradually return to its old channel.
translations.idiomatic: Upon first taking office, he asked to build many brush weirs above and below the Jinmen Sluice so the river might gradually return to its old course.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，复疏請於金門閘下增設草壩一，引永定河歸故道，自中亭、玉帶達天津歸海。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he again memorialized asking to add another brush weir below the Jinmen Sluice, divert the Yongding River back to its old course, and let it reach the sea via Zhongting and Yudai through Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he again memorialized asking to add another brush weir below the Jinmen Sluice, divert the Yongding River back to its old course, and let it reach the sea by way of Zhongting and Yudai through Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 得旨，偕總河顧琮悉心經理。

translations.literal: The directive was granted, and together with the Director-General of Rivers Gu Cong he managed the work with full care.
translations.idiomatic: The directive was granted, and together with the Director-General of Rivers Gu Cong he managed the work with full care.

sentences.zh: 嘉淦复疏言：「天津南北運河與淀河會於西沽​​以入於海河。

translations.literal: Jiagan again memorialized: 'The north and south Grand Canals at Tianjin join the Dian River at Xigu to enter the Hai River.
translations.idiomatic: Jiagan again memorialized: 'The north and south Grand Canals at Tianjin join the Dian River at Xigu to enter the Hai River.

sentences.zh: 南運河水濁，久必淤墊，況通省之水皆匯於此，秋潦時至，宣洩不及。

translations.literal: The southern canal's water is muddy and in time must silt up; moreover all the province's waters converge here, and when autumn floods come, discharge cannot keep pace.
translations.idiomatic: The southern canal's water is muddy and in time must silt up; moreover all the province's waters converge here, and when autumn floods come, discharge cannot keep pace.

sentences.zh: 大學士鄂爾泰曾奏准於靜海​​獨流疏引河，實下游治水之關鍵。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ortai once memorialized approval to dredge a diversion canal at Duliu in Jinghai—this is truly the key to managing water in the lower reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ortai once won approval to dredge a diversion canal at Duliu in Jinghai—this is truly the key to managing water in the lower reaches.

sentences.zh: 但開河易，達海難，設中途梗阻，必更漫溢為患。

translations.literal: But opening a canal is easy while reaching the sea is hard; if obstruction occurs midway, flooding must become an even greater calamity.
translations.idiomatic: But opening a canal is easy while reaching the sea is hard; if obstruction occurs midway, flooding will only grow worse.

sentences.zh: 且海口開深，又恐潮水倒灌。

translations.literal: Moreover, if the estuary is dredged too deep, one fears the tide will flow back upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if the estuary is dredged too deep, one fears the tide will flow back upstream.

sentences.zh: 臣等現勘通省水道，凡眾河交會及入淀、入海之路，有急宜修濬者，即於今夏興修。

translations.literal: Your servants have now surveyed the province's waterways; wherever major rivers meet or routes enter the marshes or the sea urgently need dredging, work shall begin this summer.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants have now surveyed the province's waterways; wherever major rivers meet or routes enter the marshes or the sea and urgently need dredging, work shall begin this summer.

sentences.zh: 」報聞。

translations.literal: ' The report was noted.
translations.idiomatic: ' The report was noted.

sentences.zh: 五月，晉太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，疏言：「直隸經流之大者，永定、子牙、南運、北運四河，與東西兩淀。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year he memorialized: 'The great trunk streams of Zhili are the Yongding, Ziya, southern Grand Canal, and northern Grand Canal—four rivers—and the eastern and western marshes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year he memorialized: 'The great trunk streams of Zhili are the Yongding, Ziya, southern Grand Canal, and northern Grand Canal—four rivers—and the eastern and western marshes.

sentences.zh: 治永​​定河，擬於葉淀之東疏引河，由西沽北入海；

translations.literal: To regulate the Yongding River, we propose dredging a diversion east of Yedian so it enters the sea north of Xigu;
translations.idiomatic: To regulate the Yongding River, we propose dredging a diversion east of Yedian so it enters the sea north of Xigu;

sentences.zh: 治子牙河，擬濬新河，引上游諸水入淀，開舊河東堤，使漸由西沽南入海；

translations.literal: to regulate the Ziya River, we propose dredging a new channel to draw upstream waters into the marshes and breach the old river's eastern embankment so it may gradually enter the sea south of Xigu;
translations.idiomatic: to regulate the Ziya River, we propose dredging a new channel to draw upstream waters into the marshes and breach the old river's eastern embankment so it may gradually enter the sea south of Xigu;

sentences.zh: 治北運河，兩岸去沙裁直，濬減河，培堤岸；

translations.literal: to regulate the northern Grand Canal, remove sand and straighten both banks, dredge relief channels, and raise the dikes;
translations.idiomatic: to regulate the northern Grand Canal, remove sand and straighten both banks, dredge relief channels, and raise the dikes;

sentences.zh: 治南運河，兩岸築遙堤，濬河使行正溜，安陵鎮建閘，濬減河三十餘裡，入老河口達於海；

translations.literal: to regulate the southern Grand Canal, build distant dikes on both banks, dredge the channel for the main current, erect a sluice at Anling Town, dredge a relief channel of more than thirty li to enter the old river mouth and reach the sea;
translations.idiomatic: to regulate the southern Grand Canal, build distant dikes on both banks, dredge the channel for the main current, erect a sluice at Anling Town, dredge a relief channel of more than thirty li to enter the old river mouth and reach the sea;

sentences.zh: 治西淀，擬開白溝河故道以入中亭，九橋南別疏一河，並濬青門河別派分流，下游已暢達，復將金門閘西引河改由東道，於苑家口疊道建木橋五，使瀝水通行；

translations.literal: to regulate the western marsh, we propose reopening the old course of the Baigou River to enter Zhongting, dredging a separate channel south of Jiuqiao, and dredging the Qingmen River's branch for diversion; the lower reaches are already unobstructed, and we further propose shifting the western diversion at Jinmen Sluice to the eastern route, building five timber bridges on a raised road at Yuanjiakou so runoff may pass;
translations.idiomatic: to regulate the western marsh, we propose reopening the old course of the Baigou River to enter Zhongting, dredging a separate channel south of Jiuqiao, and dredging the Qingmen River's branch for diversion; the lower reaches are already unobstructed, and we further propose shifting the western diversion at Jinmen Sluice to the eastern route, building five timber bridges on a raised road at Yuanjiakou so runoff may pass;

sentences.zh: 治東淀，擬濬上游三岔河令寬深，楊家河、卞家河窪諸處疏引河，並行而東會於西沽，庶使四河順軌，兩淀暢洩。

translations.literal: to regulate the eastern marsh, we propose dredging the upper Sancha River wider and deeper, opening diversion channels at Yangjia River, Bianjia River depression, and other places, all running east to meet at Xigu, so that the four rivers may follow their courses and both marshes drain freely.
translations.idiomatic: to regulate the eastern marsh, we propose dredging the upper Sancha River wider and deeper, opening diversion channels at Yangjia River, Bianjia River depression, and other places, all running east to meet at Xigu, so that the four rivers may follow their courses and both marshes drain freely.

sentences.zh: 」又引永定河改歸故道，各工俱全，上嘉之。

translations.literal: ' He also diverted the Yongding River back to its old course; when all works were complete, the Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: ' He also diverted the Yongding River back to its old course; when all works were complete, the Emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 時江南總督高斌入都，上命會同嘉淦議河務，十月，合疏言：「永定河當於固安南、霸州北順流東下，接東淀達西沽入海，則上游漲水自消。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiangnan governor-general Gao Bin came to the capital; the Emperor ordered him to confer with Jiagan on river affairs. In the tenth month they jointly memorialized: 'The Yongding River should flow east downstream south of Gu'an and north of Bazhou, join the eastern marsh, reach Xigu, and enter the sea—then the upstream flood will dissipate of itself.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Jiangnan governor-general Gao Bin came to the capital; the Emperor ordered him to confer with Jiagan on river affairs.
